articles.title: OpenAI Publishes Analysis on Model Perplexity and Intelligence Relationships
articles.description:
OpenAI published an official analysis examining the relationship between language model perplexity and intelligence, exploring how pre-training metrics correlate with modern model capabilities. The publication addresses foundational training metrics amidst ongoing industry discussions regarding scaling laws and reasoning-focused architectures.

hackernews · acossta · Nov 22, 17:06 · Discussion

「Background」 Perplexity is a standard metric used to measure how well a probability model predicts a sample, serving as a traditional evaluation of language model pre-training quality.

「Impact」 Engineers and researchers gain additional perspective on evaluating base model potential versus reinforcement learning and chain-of-thought improvements.

「Community Discussion」 Community members debated whether pre-training perplexity remains a reliable indicator of real-world capability given the performance of reasoning models like o1 and o3, with several commenters noting GPT-4.5 as a notable discontinuity on performance graphs.

Tags: `artificial intelligence`, `language models`, `machine learning research`, `scaling laws`

articles.title: Graham Dumpleton Introduces Muru, an AI-Assisted Rust Server for Python Apps
articles.description:
Mod\wsgi creator Graham Dumpleton has introduced Muru, a new AI-assisted Rust server designed for running ASGI and WSGI Python applications in both development and production environments. Between November 4 and November 22, 2026, Dumpleton published a detailed series of posts documenting the design, architecture, and implementation process of the project. Dumpleton states that while AI assists with the workload, his twenty years of experience with mod\wsgi guide the project's standards and quality control.

rss · Simon Willison · Nov 21, 23:56

「Background」 Graham Dumpleton created mod\wsgi 20 years ago, establishing a long-standing tool for serving Python web applications in production. Muru represents his subsequent effort to build an updated server utilizing Rust and AI assistance.

Tags: `Python web applications`, `Rust server`, `ASGI WSGI`, `Software development`

articles.title: To Code Well, Avoid Blunders
articles.description:
rss · Sean Goedecke · Nov 22, 00:00

「Background」 Engineers often mistakenly view programming as a pursuit of brilliant insights and clever abstractions, whereas software engineering success in large commercial codebases actually depends on preventing catastrophic mistakes.

「Solution」 Sean Goedecke argues that programming resembles chess or tennis, where avoiding major blunders—such as hanging pieces or failing to return balls—secures victory against most opponents without needing brilliant tactical moves. Because a single blunder can ruin an elegant codebase, unlike sports where a massive lead absorbs mistakes, developers must avoid cardinal sins like inconsistency and unnecessary requirements. Inconsistency breaks engineering trust by forcing developers to hunt for surprises, while unnecessary requirements are sticky, resist removal, and trigger combinatorial explosion when interacting with new features. To mitigate these risks, developers should identify how tasks fit normally into existing systems and trim requirements to the absolute minimum.
